entries.statement: PTX 9.3 defines .b32 as a fundamental type specifier whose basic type is Bits (untyped) and whose size is 32 bits.
PTX 9.3 defines registers as the .reg state space; registers may be typed or untyped, predicate registers are 1-bit, and scalar register widths include 32 bits.

Project modeling convention for this bounded core: represent each .b32 register value as an exact fixed-width 32-bit untyped bit value; this is not an NVIDIA source fact and supplies no instruction-specific numeric interpretation.
PTX 9.3 section 9.7 states that all PTX instructions may be predicated and that instruction descriptions omit the optional guard predicate.

PTX 9.3 section 9.7.13.2 states that an instruction or instruction block executes for threads whose guard predicate is true and that threads with a false guard predicate do nothing; its semantics line is 'If {!}p then instruction'.

Derived for this bounded core: when the complete optional guard expression is false, the instruction performs no transition on the modeled value-register and predicate-register state. This is a project interpretation of the official 'do nothing' clause, not NVIDIA verbatim text.

Project modeling convention for an eligible bounded unit: model instruction-local machine state as an ordinary .b32 value-register file plus a Boolean predicate-register file, and exclude every other PTX state component; this is not an NVIDIA source fact and is valid only after unit-specific scope checking confirms no excluded effect.

Project modeling convention for this bounded core: value-register and predicate-register lookup is partial; a missing required binding yields Option none and denotes execution outside the modeled well-formed lookup domain, not an NVIDIA-defined error, trap, undefined value, or invented default.
PTX 9.3 section 9.2 states that for some instructions the destination is optional and '_' may replace a destination register.

evidence.quotation: A fundamental type specifies both a basic type and a size. Register variables are always of a fundamental type, and instructions operate on these types.

Registers (.reg state space) are fast storage locations. Registers may be typed (signed integer, unsigned integer, floating point, predicate) or untyped. Register size is restricted; aside from predicate registers which are 1-bit, scalar registers have a width of 8-, 16-, 32-, 64-, or 128-bits.
All PTX instructions may be predicated. In the following descriptions, the optional guard predicate is omitted from the syntax.
Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.
For some instructions the destination operand is optional. A bit bucket operand denoted with an underscore (_) may be used in place of a destination register.

eligibilityRequirements: The unit is a scalar .b32 instruction.
Its bounded syntax reads ordinary value registers or immediate bit values and may read one predicate guard.
Its bounded state effects are confined to ordinary destination-register update or no update.
Instruction-specific legality, operation, typing compatibility, and exceptional behavior remain in the unit delta.
excludedFeatures: memory, texture, surface, atomic, barrier, concurrency, call, return, branch, and control-transfer effects
special-register, parameter, address-variable, function-address, or kernel-address semantics
vector, packed, matrix, tensor, and non-.b32 value forms
implicit flags, carry, status, condition-code, rounding, saturation, or exception state
instruction-specific permission to use the bit-bucket destination
scope.statement: PTX ISA 9.3 bounded scalar .b32 instructions whose modeled effects are confined to ordinary value registers and optional predicate guards.
